Past Perfect Continuous and Past Perfect
You do not describe states with continuous tenses - you can only use them to describe actions. Therefore, you have to use the Past Perfect to describe a state.

For example:
I had been there before.
I had been being there before.
You use the Past Perfect to focus on the length of a particular time before another time.

For example:
We had only owned the house for two months before it was ruined by flood waters.
The Past Perfect Continuous is mainly used in written texts and is less common in conversation.
His parents had been pressuring him about it for weeks to invite his second cousin Bernard over for dinner.
Finally, one day when Jerry was bored, he had decided to invite Bernard over for dinner.
When Bernard had walked in, Jerry had been shocked.
Instead, what Jerry had seen was a spry, good-looking man who had certainly looked younger than his 75 years.
When Jerry had invited him in, Bernard seemed to have been studying Jerry closely.
Jerry had been amazed at how much he had been enjoying himself when it got to dinner.
He began to tell Jerry how he had run away from home at the age of 17 with the goal of reaching Europe.
He had told his young cousin how he had been hitchhiking across Africa when he had started traveling with a tribe through the desert.
Bernard recounted how he had had adventures with Arab merchants while he had been traveling up the Nile.
Bernard had wanted to leave stories for another night.
Jerry couldn't believe how much he had been enjoying his second cousin's company.
Using a variety of structure in your written and spoken English is a good way to make yourself more interesting to read and listen to. Using the Perfect Infinitive Continuous is a good way to start.
The form of the Perfect Infinitive Continuous is:
subject + have been + present participle (verb -ing)
She seems to have been waiting for a while.
You use the Perfect Infinitive Continuous after modal verbs and after appear and seem, but it can also be used after happen, pretend and the passive of believe, know, report, say, understand.

For example:
You shouldn't have been following him closely.
He appears to have been sitting there a long time.
They pretended to have been working.
Jerry only pretended to have been listening.
He had expected to have been having dinner with an elderly man.

He understood Bernard to have been someone needing adventure. He could not imagine himself to have been traveling for such a long time and so far away.

images.text:
Jerry only pretended to have been listening. His parents had been pressuring him about it for weeks to invite his second cousin Bernard over for dinner. However, second cousin Bernard, who had lived in Seattle since he had moved from South Africa years before, was 75. Whatever would they have in common?
Finally, one day when Jerry was bored, he had decided to invite Bernard over for dinner. When Bernard had walked in, Jerry had been shocked. He had expected to have been having dinner with an elderly man. Instead, what Jerry had seen was a spry, good-looking man who had certainly looked younger than his 75 years.

When Jerry had invited him in, Bernard seemed to have been studying Jerry closely.
He said, "You look like my brother Jo. Yes, indeed. Jo had the same flaming red hair and the same strong chin."
Jerry beamed. The rest of the family had been teasing him for years because no one in the family had carroty hair. He was glad to have been finally finding out that this was in fact not true. Bernard took a seat as Jerry put out some cheese and crackers. Jerry had been amazed at how much he had been enjoying himself when it got to dinner. Bernard had turned out to be quite a character, not at all like the rest of Jerry's strait-laced family.

Over dinner, Jerry asked Bernard about his travels. "Oh, it's a very long story." Bernard was known to have been finding his own way in life. He began to tell Jerry how he had run away from home at the age of 17 with the goal of reaching Europe. He had told his young cousin how he had been hitchhiking across Africa when he had started traveling with a tribe through the desert.
Bernard recounted how he had had adventures with Arab merchants while he had been traveling up the Nile. Jerry sat mesmerized. He understood Bernard to have been someone needing adventure. He could not imagine himself to have been traveling for such a long time and so far away.

"What happened next?" Jerry had asked him. He had certainly wanted to hear more.
Bernard had wanted to leave stories for another night. Jerry couldn't believe how much he had been enjoying his second cousin's company. He had decided then and there that he would be inviting Bernard again.
